title: Identifying Fractions Worksheets: Shaded Shapes
intro: Help your student distinguish the whole, all equal parts, and shaded parts.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Point to the complete strip before counting. Record the total number of equal parts as the denominator and the shaded count as the numerator.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Ask your student

Which number tells how many equal parts make the whole?

If your student needs help

If the student counts only unshaded parts for the denominator, trace the entire strip together.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set has six original strip pictures. The wholes have 2, 3, 4, 6, or 8 equal parts, with at least one shaded part and at least one unshaded part. The answer key names the pieces shown without simplifying. These are part-of-a-whole models, not number-line questions or a complete fraction assessment.
